cmux-browser.doc: cmux-browser-mcp (github.com/jasonraz/cmux-browser-mcp): server.mjs v1.3.0, 45 tools, macOS + cmux only. The server shares one defaultSurface, so every call passes an explicit `surface`. omp device = xd://mcp__cmux_browser_<tool> (needs the cmux_browser underscoredServers entry: the doubled-token rule would otherwise split browser_open at browser_ / open). Claude name = mcp__cmux-browser__<tool>. subagentAllow is the only set a subagent may call; sensitive tools expose cookies, storage, page JS, request bodies or files and are lead-only.
cmux-browser.install: git clone https://github.com/jasonraz/cmux-browser-mcp && cd cmux-browser-mcp && ./install.sh  (then: claude mcp add cmux-browser --scope user -- node ~/.claude/mcp-servers/cmux-browser/server.mjs; omp: add the same stdio command under mcpServers in ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json)

note: Two lists with different purposes; do not merge. connectorWatch = servers named by hooks/hooks.json's connector_credential_watch.py matcher, longest prefix first (read by omp/hook-bridge.ts CONNECTOR_SERVERS). underscoredServers = servers whose underscored names break xd://mcp__<server>_<tool> boundary guessing, longest match wins (read by scripts/omp_transcript.py). atlas_connectwise is listed explicitly because its tools are cw_* (mcp__atlas_connectwise_cw_status), so the doubled-token rule cannot find the boundary; every other atlas connector repeats its server token (atlas_falcon_falcon_*) and is found by that rule; mcp_search is the claude-mem plugin's server. Both readers fall back to their built-in literal if this file is unreadable; parity tests pin them.
